definitions.explanation: A bottle that has been emptied of its contents. Commonly encountered in the context of recycling and waste separation in Japan.

examples.japanese: {空|あ}き{瓶|びん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{洗|あら}う→洗う：00827_arau⟧。
{空|あ}き{瓶|びん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{資源|しげん}ごみ→資源ごみ：09537_shigengomi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}して→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please put empty bottles out with the recyclables.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{隅|すみ}→隅：01625_sumi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{空|あ}き{瓶|びん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{転|ころ}がっていた→転がる：02571_korogaru⟧。
examples.english: There were many empty bottles lying around in the corner of the yard.

notes: Composed of ⟦{空|あ}き→空く：11062_aku⟧ (empty, vacant) + ⟦{瓶|びん}→瓶：01016_bin⟧ (bottle). Part of a series with ⟦{空|あ}き{缶|かん}→空き缶：23052_akikan⟧ (empty can) and ⟦{空|あ}き→空き：10464_aki⟧{箱|ばこ} (empty box). In Japanese garbage separation systems, {空|あ}き{瓶|びん} are typically classified as ⟦{資源|しげん}ごみ→資源ごみ：09537_shigengomi⟧ (recyclable waste) and collected separately. The prefix ⟦{空|あ}き→空く：11062_aku⟧- is productive: ⟦{空|あ}き{家|や}→空き家：03007_akiya⟧ (vacant house), ⟦{空|あ}き{地|ち}→空き地：15270_akichi⟧ (vacant lot), ⟦{空|あ}き→空き：10464_aki⟧⟦{室|しつ}→室：09946_shitsu⟧ (vacant room).
